CORPORATE 
 
Yulefest Kilkenny 2023 
Yulefest Kilkenny 2023 began on November 25th, with Santa’s arrival to the City switching on of the new 
Christmas Lights and the opening of the Yulefest Christmas Market. 
 
Yulefest Kilkenny 2023 was a spectacular celebration of the festive season from November 25th right through 
to December 22nd. The festivities commenced with the exciting arrival of Santa Claus who not only lit up 
the City with his magical presence but also illuminated the streets with the switch-on of the new Christmas 
Lights. Yulefest Christmas Market officially opened its gates, inviting locals and visitors alike to get into the 
holiday spirit. 
 
Throughout the festival, people were treated to an array of festive treats, creative crafts and live music at 
the weekend Christmas Market and Yulefest Bandstand. Special events dotted each weekend, ensuring 
there was never a dull moment. The City sparkled with new festive Christmas lights. Across the County, 
Santa made appearances, spreading the Christmas spirit in every corner. 
 
This year's featured events were spectacular. The Medieval Mile Run on December 1st kicked off the 
physical festivities, while the Santa Truck brought its unique brand of cheer on December 9th. The Yulefest 
Movie Night on Thursday the 14th provided a cinematic escape followed by the fabulous Rogu Fire Show 
on the 16th. The festival reached its finale with the Festive Friday on December 22nd, featuring a dazzling 
display of fireworks, live music, the bustling Christmas Market and family entertainment. 
 
 
 
 
The Yulefest Bandstand serenaded the City with live music every Saturday, while The Parade became a hub 
for family entertainment every Sunday. Santa Experiences, Markets across the County, Music Concerts and 
Art Workshops added to the festive appeal, ensuring that joy and Christmas cheer echoed throughout 
Kilkenny's City and County.

National Deposit Return Scheme 
Ireland will soon be introducing a Deposit Return Scheme. In February 2024, when you buy a drink in a 
plastic bottle, aluminium or steel can that features the Re-turn logo, you pay a small deposit in addition to 
the price of the drink. When you return your empty, undamaged container to any retail outlet, you get your 
deposit back in full. (Details at https://re-turn.ie/). 
 
National Brown Bin Collection Scheme 
From January 2024, new EU legislation means every household will be entitled to avail of a brown bin 
collection service. Approximately 69% of households in Ireland up until now, are able to avail of a food 
waste collection service from their waste service collector. MyWaste.ie is encouraging everyone, here, there, 
and everywhere to contact their waste collector and request a brown bin service in 2024, because “you’re 
never too remote to recycle!” (Details https://www.mywaste.ie/brown-bin-service/)

into the sale, transport and production of Solid

These inspections involved compiling a list of all

County. The new Solid Fuel Regulations state it is 
illegal to sell or transport bituminous coal in the 
Republic of Ireland.  
 
Each premises from this list was sent an advisory

inspection taking place.  Each inspection involved 
inspecting the products for the following criteria: 
 
(a) 
The correct product.

The product was packaged and labelled 
correctly with the appropriate regulatory 
language in place.

The supplier is registered with the EPA.

Kilkenny Countryside Park 
A big crowd turned out to mark the official 
opening of the new Kilkenny Countryside Park at 
Dunmore on Friday, 15th December.

Heritage & Electoral Reform in the presence of the 
Cathaoirleach of Kilkenny County Council, Cllr. 
Michael Doyle and Mayor of Kilkenny City, Cllr. 
Joe Malone.  
 
This project sees the development of a new 
countryside park on the site of the closed 
municipal landfill at Dunmore, which occupies an 
area of circa. 24 acres and is located just 5km north 
of Kilkenny City Centre. The new park offers 
visitors three themed trails, the Mass Path Trail, 
which starts at Dunmore village along with an 
Accessibility Trail and a Biodiversity Trail. The 
new Park also provides a myriad of other 
attractions, including two ball walls, a bespoke 
viewing area, play and exercise equipment and 
novel relaxing spaces that include hammocks, and

Conservation 
The Conservation Office manages all protected 
structures in Kilkenny County and City. These 
structures are recognised for their Architectural, 
Historical, Archaeological, Artistic, Cultural, 
Scientific, Technical, Social special interest. An 
advisory service on conservation matters is 
provided to the public and colleagues, while the 
conservation grants and funding applications are 
also delivered. 
 
Conservation Grants 2024 were launched in 
November, they include:  
 
Built Heritage Investment Scheme (BHIS) 2024 
The aim of the Built Heritage Investment Scheme 
is to investment in a significant number of small-
scale, labour-intensive conservation projects 
throughout the County and to support the 
employment 
of 
conservation 
professionals, 
craftspeople and tradespersons in the repair of the 
historic built environment. Kilkenny’s grant 
allocation is €156,800.  
 
Historic Structures Fund (HSF) 2024 
Funding for the Historic Structures Fund (HSF) is 
being made available as part of Project Ireland 
2040. The primary focus of the Historic Structures 
Fund will be on conservation and enhancement of 
historic structures and buildings for the broader 
benefit of communities and the public. 
 
Stream 1 will offer grants from €15,000 up to 
€50,000 
Stream 2 will offer a small number of grants from 
€50,000 up to €200,000 
Vernacular Structures Stream – In the context of A 
Living Tradition: A Strategy to Enhance the 
Understanding, Minding and Handing on of Our 
Built Vernacular Heritage (2021), the stream for 
vernacular structures is being retained for 2024, 
with funding of €150,000. 
 
The purpose of the stream is to support 
conservation repairs and small capital works to 
vernacular structures that are not listed in Local 
Authority Records of Protected Structures or

RENT-A-ROOM SCHEME 
The Rent-a-Room scheme has been extended to local authority tenancies.  
The broad outline of how the Scheme will to operate is as follows: 
 
▪ 
The local authority tenant advertises an available room - gov.ie/roomforastudent provides information 
to those wishing to rent a room to students in full time education, along with information for students.  
▪ 
Once the tenant and the student are happy to proceed, they apply to the local authority for consent for 
the duration of the academic year. 
▪ 
The local authority may decide to carry out a Garda check in respect of the student. 
▪ 
The local authority has discretion to approve or refuse the application. 
▪ 
Grounds for non-approval include, but are not limited to: 
▪ 
Rent arrears without a payment plan; 
▪ 
Overcrowding; 
▪ 
Anti-social behaviour or on good estate management grounds; 
▪ 
The property is unsuitable on other grounds e.g. size, condition, access, facilities, etc.  
▪ 
The tenants may charge and receive a rent from the student – such rental income will be considered 
reckonable income under the local authority’s Differential Rent Scheme, with rent charged by the local 
authority according to that scheme. 
▪ 
The student will not be included on the tenant’s rent account, that is any income generated by the 
student renting a room will not be assessable for differential rent purposes.  
▪ 
The tenant is ultimately responsible for any breach of the tenancy agreement by any member of their 
household, and if necessary the local authority may issue a tenancy warning for any such breach.  
▪ 
At the end of the academic year, the student must vacate the property. Should the tenant and student 
wish to continue the arrangement into the next academic year, consent of the local authority is required.

Affordable Homes: 
Kilkenny County Council, in collaboration with CAIRN, will be advertising an Affordable Purchase Scheme 
of 3-bedroom homes at Nyne Park, Kilkenny City, set to launch in Q1 2024.  
 
The marketing campaign for this first Affordable Purchase Scheme has commenced.    The Council has 
placed a general advertisement in the Kilkenny People in the lead up to Christmas advising that Affordable 
Housing in Kilkenny City is coming soon.   The Council has also initiated a social media campaign over the 
Christmas period.  This will increase over the month of January.  
 
In tandem, CAIRN has developed an information webpage on the scheme https://www.cairnhomes.com/nyne-
park/.  In addition, they have placed billboards in key locations around the City along with digiboard 
advertising in MacDonagh Junction. During the month of January, they will be building on their marketing. 
 
It is expected that the scheme will be advertised later in January.  Application will be via an online portal 
only, with the portal for applications opening in February.  The Scheme will be advertised publicly via the 
Council’s website, Social Media channels and via print media. 
 
The Affordable Housing Team are continuing to prepare for the roll out of this scheme.   
Under the Local Authority Affordable Purchase Scheme, Kilkenny County Council will make homes 
available at a reduced price for eligible applicants who are seeking to purchase a newly built home but need 
additional funds to bridge the gap between their mortgage and deposit to cover the full price of the 
home.  In return, Kilkenny County Council will take a percentage Equity Share in the Affordable 
Home.  Purchasers will enter into an Affordable Dwelling Purchase Agreement with Kilkenny County

VACANT HOMES 
The Vacant Properties Refurbishment Grant, Croí Cónaithe is one of the measures in order to address 
vacancy and efficient use of existing stock in Housing for All.  The grant is aimed at bringing vacant and 
derelict properties back into residential use.  The scheme was originally for people who were refurbishing 
vacant properties for use as their principal private residence.  The Government has announced that as of 
1st May 2023, there will be a number of changes to this scheme including that the scheme will be expanded 
to property owners who wish to refurbish their vacant property for rental purposes.   The detail and 
guidance regarding the modified scheme have not yet been issued by the Department of Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage.   There has been a substantial increase in the number of calls to the Housing 
Department regarding this scheme and a register of all inquiries to the Council will be kept for follow up 
when further details of the revised scheme are available.  
 
All queries in relation to this grant should be submitted by email to Vacanthomes@Kilkennycoco.ie and will 
be responded to in a timely manner.

New Commercial Rates Legislation: 
Following the recent and impending commencement of a number of Sections of the "Local Government 
Rates Other Matters Act 2019”, several important changes are taking place in 2024, the most significant 
of which are: 
 
▪ 
Removal of the two moieties payment dates and replacement with a single charge for the year. 
 
▪ 
Rates now due in full, on issue of demand. 
 
▪ 
Interest charges falling due on any unpaid rates balance at year end, this will be effective from 
January 2025. Interest will be applied in 2026 on unpaid 2025 rate bills. 
 
What do these changes mean for Rate Payers?  
 
Removal of the Two Moieties 
In previous years, Commercial Rates were payable in two moieties (halves), with the first 50% (plus any 
arrears due) being due on issue of the demand, and the second 50% falling due on the 1st July.  Commercial 
Rates are now payable in full from 1st January, 2024. Commercial rate payers will be required therefore 
to make payment of the full amount (and any arrears due) upon receipt of your Rates bill. 
 
Alternatively, the cost of the Commercial Rates can be paid over 9 months of the year by availing of 
Direct Debit option.
